steps.content: Forensica stares blankly into space. Her eyes are calm, and she appears to be lost in thought. You notice her fingers gripping the pocket of her clothes.
She's remained uncooperative ever since her arrest, refusing to answer any questions.
By now, you can make out the shape of the object from it being pressed against the pocket—it's a pinky bone.
Let me introduce myself. I'm the Chief of the MBCC, and I'm in charge of your interrogation for this case.
Forensica doesn't move, but her gaze sharpens as it falls on you. You know that look. It's wariness, one you'd find in a cornered animal. She looks you up and down, sizing you up.
Despite never having met before, she seems to be extremely hostile towards you. She keeps her mouth shut, repulsion written all over her face.
Body theft may not be a serious crime, but it still involves endangering public safety and desecrating human remains.
I heard you used to be a forensic pathologist. You should understand the charges better than I do.
When you mention her work as a forensic pathologist, Forensica can't help but slip her hand into her pocket.
You notice the movement, and the finger bone is now partially visible at the edge of her pocket.
Do you have anything to say about what you've done?
...Or rather, is there anything I can help you with?
Forensica lets out a cold laugh and finally speaks, her tone extremely sharp.

steps.speaker: Forensica
steps.content: Help me? You hypocrites would be doing me a great favor already if you'd just go far, far away.
So you do need help.

steps.speaker: Forensica
steps.content: It's one thing to listen to people's dying wishes, it's another to pry into private memories. Going deeper requires strong persistence. Since I don't have any, I can't fulfill your request.
It seems her wariness isn't directed at you specifically, but rather a certain group of people.
The records show that Forensica used to work at a forensic examination center before being dismissed for certain reasons.
These days, while she might appear to be an empty shell, she never actually gave up on forensic examination and related work.
In order to make a living, she became Clementine's consultant, providing expertise in forensics for her novels.
She's exactly as described in Clementine's novels—eccentric, peculiar, and guarded.
Perhaps it's because the novel's portrayal was so vivid. Even though she should be a complete stranger, you feel as if you've known her for ages.
This sense of familiarity intrigues you, and makes you more patient. You want to understand what Forensica is truly thinking.
If you don't want to talk about the case, we can discuss something else.
How's Dorothy doing?

steps.speaker: Forensica
steps.content: ...I don't know what you're talking about.
You take out the bestselling book, "Murder on the Praeva Express," and set it in front of her.
I'm sure you know this book—you're basically the same person in and outside of it.
We may have never met in person, but we made quite a good combo in Clementine's novel, didn't we?
In the story, we worked together to find the killer. As a token of our friendship, you gave me a finger bone.
That finger bone came from your collection. Dorothy, if I recall correctly.

steps.speaker: Seconds drag by before the presence retreats into the distance. You lift your gaze and find Chengxiao's masked face above you, the corner of his mouth tilted faintly upward.
steps.content: You know Clementine?
More than that, we've had many in-depth conversations.
Clementine mentioned how all the forensic expertise in her novels came from you. She even went as far as to say that you're her most trusted consultant.
Forensica reaches out and closes the novel you had opened. The dust jacket is covered in highly positive reviews and recommendations.

steps.speaker: Forensica
steps.content: That woman... I suppose she's a decent novelist. At least she respects the facts.
Whether it's because of Clementine, or because you acknowledged the novel, Forensica's hostility, while not entirely gone, has noticeably diminished.
Clementine holds you in very high regard, you know. She said you're a rare genius whose knowledge and intuition far surpass the ordinary.

steps.speaker: Forensica
steps.content: A genius? I highly doubt a real genius would end up being locked up in a place like this, waiting to be judged.

steps.speaker: Forensica
steps.content: What exactly are you getting at anyway? Are you trying to approach me as the same character that's in the novel? Or are you just trying to brag about how much you read?
I was trying to bridge the gap between us. Doesn't seem to be working, though.
That said, we did work together to find the killer in the novel. Perhaps we can do the same now.
You pull up the files on the various charges against Forensica. Nearly every single one points to her investigating something.
I just want to know why you did this. Are you investigating the truth behind a particular case?

steps.speaker: Forensica
steps.content: Truth? As if such a thing exists.

steps.speaker: Forensica
steps.content: Everyone just wants to close a case, bury the body, and move on as quickly as possible. That's the only "truth."

steps.speaker: Forensica
steps.content: Everyone has their own agenda in this world. Whoever holds the power gets to decide what "truth" is.
You seem to have struck a nerve. Forensica grows increasingly agitated, her choice of words becoming much harsher.
You should know that we found the truth behind the arson case about the orphanage.

steps.speaker: Forensica
steps.content: So what? If you'd found the truth sooner, Clementine wouldn't have had to write that novel in the first place.

steps.speaker: Forensica
steps.content: Clementine wouldn't be who she is today, and her friends would still be alive.

steps.speaker: Forensica
steps.content: Bloated institutions full of red tape, breeding nothing but parasites and incompetent trash... What right does a system like that have to pass judgment on anything?
Society requires us to follow due process, but that doesn't mean we can't pursue the truth.
Gathering evidence takes time. As a forensic pathologist, you should understand that better than anyone.

steps.speaker: Forensica
steps.content: It's BECAUSE I'm a forensic pathologist that I know just how idiotic that "due process" is!

steps.speaker: Forensica
steps.content: The evidence is right there in front of us, yet people abuse their authority to manipulate procedures and turn justice into nothing but empty words!
Forensica glares at you, her hand curled tightly in her pocket, the fabric of her clothes trembling slightly from the force of her grip.
And I'm guessing that's why you refuse to work with any forensic institutions now?
Your file shows you had an outstanding academic record at DisCity University's School of Forensic Science, but your employment history after graduation...
Seven jobs in five years, and every single one ended in conflict with your superiors or colleagues.

steps.speaker: Forensica
steps.content: Don't even get me started on those idiots! They could barely get basic autopsy procedures right, and yet they can't stand having anyone correct them!

steps.speaker: Forensica
steps.content: Clumsy, careless, treating the dead like they don't matter... I was only pointing out their mistakes! What's so wrong with that?
There's nothing wrong with pointing out mistakes, but workplaces do need certain rules to be in place if they are to function properly, and...

steps.speaker: Forensica
steps.content: What, so we should favor those rules over truth and evidence?
Forensica's eyes darken, making no attempt to hide her displeasure.
That's not what I meant.

steps.speaker: Forensica
steps.content: Then are you questioning my abilities? I'll have you know, I'm the best forensic pathologist in DisCity—no, in the entire world.

steps.speaker: Forensica
steps.content: Tch. Can we just get this over with already? I don't have time to waste on idiots.
Truth and evidence are fragile. Sometimes, rules aren't obstacles—they're tools. When used properly, they can help the truth surface faster.

steps.speaker: Forensica
steps.content: Hooray, more pretty speeches. Just what I needed.

steps.speaker: Forensica
steps.content: Let me guess, now you're going to say "procedures exist for a reason," right? Or how "adapting to society is important?"

steps.speaker: Forensica
steps.content: All you and those so-called guardians of order do is put on airs, looking down from your pedestals, acting all benevolent when you're not.

steps.speaker: Forensica
steps.content: If you've ever seen a real corpse, looked into those cloudy, lifeless eyes of someone who died with unfinished business... you'd understand. Hypocrisy is far more revolting than even malevolence.
You can see a complex array of emotions across Forensica's face—fury at unjust authority, and grief for those who died with wrongs unavenged.

She despises rigid rules and convoluted legal procedures, yet she hasn't abandoned her work as a forensic pathologist. She still operates by her own code, helping anyone who needs someone to speak for the dead.
It shows that deep down, she holds something sacred. A conviction strong enough to keep her going no matter what stands in her way.

Was it this case? The one that made you lose faith in the justice system?
Forensica's expression shifts in an instant.
She stares at the file as though it were something vile.
The crime scene where you stole the corpse from was staged exactly like the Origami Killer's previous cases.
Back then, you suspected a case to be the work of them, but you couldn't get authorization from your institution or the victim's family. You tried to perform an unauthorized autopsy and got caught.
From that day forward, you were branded a problematic forensic pathologist and got blacklisted from ever practicing officially again.

steps.speaker: Forensica
steps.content: How do you have this...?
Forensica asks in a low voice, and you can hear her teeth grinding.

steps.speaker: Forensica
steps.content: And? Are you pitying me? Mocking me? Or are you planning to use this against me?

options: I want to understand the truth.

choices.text: I want to understand the truth.

steps.speaker: Forensica
steps.content: Help me? What, are you going to use your privileges as MBCC Chief and lead a bunch of freak Sinners on a rampage to hunt down the killer or something?

steps.speaker: Forensica
steps.content: Hahaha, don't make me laugh. What do you even know? All you people do is make empty promises.

steps.speaker: Forensica
steps.content: The truth... Yeah, if it weren't for the truth, I wouldn't have ended up like this either.

steps.speaker: Forensica
steps.content: And why should I give you the truth just because you asked? I didn't see anyone giving me the truth when I wanted it!
I understand that I can't earn your trust overnight.
But as a forensic pathologist who is able to draw conclusions based on objective facts and scientific evidence, you should have grounds to believe me.

steps.speaker: Forensica
steps.content: And what would that be? Your superpowers?
We both played a role in solving the orphanage arson case, and our work was recognized by the renowned author Clementine. I believe that demonstrates my ability to uncover the truth.

steps.speaker: Forensica
steps.content: ...I suppose you're right.
And secondly, there's this.

options: Autopsy consent form and morgue key

choices.text: Autopsy consent form and morgue key

steps.speaker: Forensica
steps.content: This is...
A postmortem examination requested under the Bureau's authority. Mania infection may cause unusual changes in corpses that require further autopsy to confirm.
It's all by the book.
I'm certain you need these. You don't have to trust me, but you can feel free to use me. Use my position, and my authority.
Isn't it your wish to find the evidence and truth you're looking for through autopsy?
Forensica falls silent for a long time. She lowers her head to look at her hands, her fingers tracing the outline of the bone in her pocket.
She murmurs, though it's unclear who she's speaking to.

steps.speaker: Forensica
steps.content: Why? Why would you go this far...

steps.speaker: Forensica
steps.content: What do you want from me? I have nothing I can give you...

steps.speaker: Forensica
steps.content: The truth... Is there someone in this world who actually cares about the truth?

steps.speaker: Forensica
steps.content: Sometimes, even I wonder... does truth really exist? And even if I do find it, what difference does it make?
Forensica stares at the files of the Origami Killer. She's been trapped in this case for far too long.

Because of this case, she was blacklisted from the industry, spent her days holed up in a basement, cut off contact with her parents to avoid dragging anyone else down, was hunted by forces in the shadows, and even wandered into a contamination zone, becoming a Sinner.
Because of this case, her life was torn apart.
Forensica has often felt that she's not just fighting the killer. The massive power structure, as monstrous as any beast, is also standing against her.

steps.speaker: Forensica
steps.content: Why are you doing all this?

steps.speaker: Forensica
steps.content: It'd be much easier for you to just follow protocol—put me on trial, convict me, and lock me away.

steps.speaker: Forensica
steps.content: Disturbing public safety and desecrating corpses... these are trivial charges, really.

steps.speaker: Forensica
steps.content: Especially when you consider how terrible my record is already.
What I want isn't submission. It's the truth.
If you're willing to complete the autopsy under my supervision, you can continue using me.
I believe I've shown you enough to prove that my value to you is extremely high. Am I wrong?
The confusion in Forensica's eyes gradually gives way to resolve. She takes a deep breath. It seems that she's made a decision.

steps.speaker: Forensica
steps.content: Fine. I'll accept your offer.
Tomorrow morning, nine o'clock. I'll see you at the morgue.
You rise to leave, but Forensica's voice stops you.

steps.speaker: Forensica
steps.content: In the novel... did I really give you the finger bone?
Yes. You said it was your good luck charm.
Take us away! You should get us out of here!
Forensica doesn't speak another word. The corners of her mouth subtly curl up, barely visible.
She extends her pinky and hooks it around the finger bone jutting from her pocket, her eyes brimming with anticipation for tomorrow's autopsy.
